text:
morgan: Quick thought — propose a staged datahand-off for airgapped upgrades to reduce the need to transfer full images.

sophia: What do you mean by datahand-off? like chunked bundles? :thinking_face: 

morgan: Yeah. Instead of a monolithic bundle, ship a small bootstrapping image + signed 'delta chains' that can be applied incrementally. less bandwidth, easier resume.

alex: Love that. How do we handle verification and supply-chain proofing for incremental chunks? we need to avoid TOCTOU attacks.

morgan: Each chunk is content-addressed + signed by builder key. manifest contains chain of hashes. verification is: verify signature on manifest, then verify chunk hashes match manifest before apply.

priya: Can we get an example manifest snippet? would help onboard security review.

morgan: ```
---
version: 1
boot: sha256:abc123
chunks:
  - id: 1
    sha256: def456
    sig: sig1
  - id: 2
    sha256: ghi789
    sig: sig2
```

sophia: Any fallback if a chunk is corrupted mid-apply? we should avoid leaving system in half-applied state.

morgan: Plan: transactional layering. apply each chunk to a staging mount, run integrity + smoke checks, then swap symlink. If failure, roll back staging and report.

eng-bot: deploy-artifact-uploader: artifact 1923456789-chunk-1 uploaded to s3-compatible store (checksum def456)

alex: We also need key rotation: builder key rotation must be handled without invalidating historical manifests. maybe include signerHistory metadata and a verification chain.

priya: Regulated customers will want HSM integration and audit log of signing ops.

sophia: Can the bootstrap image include a "fetcher" that understands mirrors and resume logic? e.g., fallback to usb media.

morgan: Yep. fetcher will support multi-source + retry + partial resume. command example:
```
redwood-fetch --manifest https://local-mirror/mf.json --dest /tmp/staging
```

alex: Also consider a small proof-of-apply token that the node sends back to operator (signed) so we have attestation of success.

priya: Sounds good. I'll draft a follow-up RFC with attacker models and rollback diagrams. tagging @sophia for API boundaries.

sophia: Thanks. please include timeline estimates and an explicit "minimum safe bootstrap" surface so support can test.

morgan: Will do. starting draft today :memo:
